newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt calms depositors after finance suspension.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt calms depositors after finance suspension.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi on Wednesday assured investors that all deposits at non-suspended finance companies and commercial banks were fully insured.

"We, as government, would provide unconditional guarantees of all deposits, and creditors (of financial institutions), when they mature, in all cases. The public should not panic or be confused (by rumours)," Thanong said.
The officials gave the assurance after meeting with representatives of 15 commercial banks and 33 non-suspended finance firms at the Bank of Thailand.

The assurance came one day after the government announced the suspension of 42 cash-strapped finance firms for at least three months while they worked on revival plans. Another 16 firms were suspended in late June.
The government said on Tuesday that creditors and depositors of the troubled firms would be fully protected.
"Right now there is a lack of confidence among some depositors, leading to fund withdrawals (from some financial institutions)," Chaiyawat said.
"If there is no confidence from the people and nobody wants to deposit money with financial institutions, we won't have any financial institutions left in Thailand," he said.
The Thai bourse fell more than two percent in the morning on concerns over the finance sector.
Chaiyawat also warned branch managers of some local commercial banks who were making negative comments about other banks' financial health in a bid to lure deposits.
"The central bank has already mentioned this to all commercial bank executives. They promised that there will be no such actions (of false allegations) any more," the governor said.
Thanong said Thailand had also obtained numerous offers of credit lines from many major foreign commercial lenders.

"I can say that many world-class banks have offered us emergency credit lines, but we still have our own resources. Money is not the problem. The issue is for us to be united and not panic," he said, referring to jitters about the stability of Thailand's financial institutions.
A senior official at Sakura Bank Ltd, one of Thailand's top creditor banks, said he could not confirm any specific amount of credit lines offered by foreign banks.
"We would be glad to consider (offering credit lines) once we receive a request from the Thai government," said Nobuo Nakayama, joint general manager of Sakura Bank Ltd in Bangkok.
"But we could not present any specific amount of such credit line unless (Bangkok) makes clear the purpose of the loan and what kind of form it will take, and how the loan will be repaid," he said.

Olarn Chaiprawat, the president of the Thai Bankers' Association, assured depositors at commercial banks and non-suspended finance firms they would receive their deposits in full plus interest on the due date after the authorities' guarantee.
